```{r,echo=FALSE}
# sqrt(x+a) = b
a = sample(1:9,1)*sample(c(-1,1),1)
b = sample(2:10,1)

eq = paste0("\\sqrt{x+",a,"}=",b)
eq = gsub("+-","-",eq,fixed=T)

x = b^2-a

eq2 = paste0("x+",a,"=",b^2)
eq2 = gsub("+-","-",eq2,fixed=T)

if(a>0){
    wrd = paste0("Subtract ",abs(a)," from both sides.")
} else {
    wrd = paste0("Add ",abs(a)," to both sides.")
}


eq3 = paste0("\\sqrt{",x,"+",a,"}\\stackrel{?}{=}",b)
eq3 = gsub("+-","-",eq3,fixed=T)

```

Question
========

Find the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation.

$$`r eq`$$

Solution
========

Square both sides.

$$`r eq2`$$

`r wrd`

$$x=`r x`$$

Check the solution in the original equation.

$$`r eq3`$$

$$\sqrt{`r x+a`}=`r b`$$

Yup, that is true. So $x=`r x`$ is a solution to the given equation.

============
extype: num
exsolution: `r x`
